task: Add an Alembic data-repair migration that decodes double-encoded MS Teams credential_values and backfills unique aliases on rows corrupted by c3d4e5f6a7b8, and correct c3d4e5f6a7b8 itself.

key_reasoning.reason: The root cause is verified and the decode expression is proven locally. Several design decisions are still open: what to do with recovered assistant ids that are stale or not owned by the project (locally all of them would fail validate_ms_teams_request, so AC1 could still fail), the format of a deterministic alias that is unique per check_alias_unique and avoids SUBSYSTEM_MANAGED_PREFIXES, downgrade semantics (no-op versus re-encode), whether user_id/created_by stay NULL, and how to edit an already-published migration.

The closest pattern is the existing raw-SQL data migrations that use op.get_bind() plus logging and are tested with a mocked op (d9e8f7a6b5c4, k5l6m7n8o9p0). That covers the mechanics but not the new parts: generating collision-free aliases across all credential types per project, and making the repair idempotent on healthy and mixed-shape rows. It rewrites data on about 51 production rows with no realistic rollback. It also edits a published migration and changes what the Teams bot receives. There is no DB-backed migration test harness, which is how Defect B shipped. Base M, bumped to L for the data-migration red flag.

About 2 modified files (c3d4e5f6a7b8 and its test) and 2 new ones (the repair revision and its test), across src/external/alembic/versions and tests/codemie/migrations. Base S, bumped to M for the data-migration red flag.

Confined to the Alembic migration layer: one new revision on the single head y1z2a3b4c5d6 plus a corrective edit to c3d4e5f6a7b8. Settings model, validator, transfer service and Teams bot are only read, not changed.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M to L: requires data migration (repair of corrupted production settings rows)
File Change Estimate bumped from S to M: requires data migration
